To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the IDP theory is valid, at least for the countries in our sample; (ii) the IDP is a good tool to predict the future of the Portuguese economy in terms of inward and outward investment; (iii) the IDP model has a high explanatory power; (iv) Portugal is in the second stage of IDP and it is moving to the third one, which is characterized by an increasing share of outward investment.

the investment position of Portugal, as a small, open, peripheral economy, is consistent with IDP theory, although the country is still far from reaching the stage of maturity, and that the investment position is positively related to the economic development of the country.
the IDP hypothesis is confirmed, although not in all the stages predicted.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) the relationship between the outward and the inward investment position of a small economy, (b) the role played by the economic development of the host country in attracting inward investments, (c) the impact of the economic development of a small economy on its outward investment position, (d) the impact of other variables, such as the level of economic development of the source country and the geographical distance between source and host countries, in the outward and inward investment position of Portugal,
a theoretical and empirical analysis of the IDP hypothesis for the Portuguese case.
the following question: how does Portugal position itself in the world economy, in terms of foreign direct investments?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IDP theory is a useful tool to understand the evolution of FDI in Portugal.
the IDP hypothesis is not rejected for Portugal, and the country seems to be on its way to reach stage 3 of IDP.
Portugal has been following the path that the IDP theory would predict for a middle-income country, with some peculiarities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the last years, Portugal has been following a pattern of development that is similar to the one predicted by the IDP model.
, as expected by the theory, in a long-term perspective the Portuguese outward investment position has been rising, while the inward one has been falling, although the latter has been more intense.
, as the Portuguese economy has been growing, it has been also more integrated in the international economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Portugal is in a stage that can be characterized by a transition from the early stages of IDP to the intermediate ones.

, in spite of the fact that Portuguese economy has been experiencing significant changes in its economic structure and its insertion into the world economy, the country still has a long way to go to catch up with the most advanced countries in terms of inward and outward FDI flows.
